Semantic Topics in LLM Reasoning Traces

The corpus is the thinking column of the LLM results: one reasoning trace per student profile. dedupe() drops blanks, keeps one row per distinct trace, and records each trace’s original frequency in n.

traces <- rio::import("For_LLM-results.csv")
corpus <- dedupe(traces$thinking)
nrow(corpus)
## [1] 95

Four ways to cut a trace, one comparison

A trace runs to a few thousand words, far past what a sentence encoder reads before truncating. compare_topics() fits every candidate topic count on four units at once: the whole document, and its sentences, clauses, and phrases. Segments longer than the model’s window are re-split, tiny shards are merged into a neighbour, and numeral-only fragments are dropped. One table, one plot.

comparison <- compare_topics(
  corpus$text,
  n_topics = c(4, 6, 8, 10, 12),
  segment = c("document", "sentence", "clause", "phrase"),
  max_tokens = 200,
  merge_below = 4,
  min_content = 0.5,
  n_representatives = 5,
  cores = 4
)
comparison

## Fitted models retained: fitted(x, n_topics = 6, segment = "sentence")
plot(comparison)

Read the coherence panel first: it asks whether a topic’s top terms actually co-occur in its units. Diversity asks whether the topics share their vocabulary or own it, and explained variance always rises with more topics, so it is a sanity check rather than a criterion. The document line is the truncated view; the three segment lines model the traces in full.

The same six topics, four ways

type = "fit" on the comparison draws the per-topic report for every level’s six-topic model: count, class-based TF-IDF, and beta term bars beside the units nearest each centroid. One figure per level, same layout, so the segmentations can be read against each other.

plot(comparison, type = "fit", n_topics = 6, n_terms = 6, n_representatives = 4)

The model

fitted() takes the chosen count and level straight out of the comparison, with no refitting.

topic_model <- fitted(comparison, n_topics = 6, segment = "sentence")
topic_model
## <sbert_topic_model>
##   documents: 95 
##   segments: 8422 (sentence level) 
##   topics: 6
##   model: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
##   algorithm: deterministic k-means (Lloyd)
##   topic sizes: 2495, 1919, 1274, 1130, 1063, 541
##   between/total SS: 22.0%
summary(topic_model)

Size on three scales

Segments per topic, source traces per topic, and traces weighted by how often each was repeated in the raw file. A trace counts in every topic one of its sentences lands in, so document proportions need not sum to one.

plot(topic_model, type = "sizes")

topic_sizes(topic_model, by = "document", weights = corpus$n)

Two keyword views, one topic

sort_by = "beta" orders each topic’s words by how often the topic uses them, the generative view. The default class-based TF-IDF score promotes words this topic uses and the others do not, the discriminative view. A topic is characterised by the pair.

The topics at a glance

plot(topic_model, type = "terms")

The fit report clips its text. representatives() ranks the fitted sentences by distinctiveness margin and names the trace and position each one came from.

representatives(topic_model, n = 2)

Where to go from here

predict() assigns new traces sentence by sentence with the same segmentation, topic_membership() grades each sentence across topics, and reduce_topics() merges the six down to fewer while keeping every verb above.
